high.title: [OCP Asia-Pacific Summit Next Month: Major AI Companies to Showcase New Products — TSMC, Hon Hai, and Taiwan Tech Giants to Participate]
high.summary: The 2026 OCP (Open Compute Project) Asia-Pacific Summit is scheduled for August 11–12 in Taiwan, marking the second consecutive year the event is held on the island — underscoring Taiwan's critical role as a global AI infrastructure hub. Key Taiwan-listed participants include **TSMC (2330)**, **Hon Hai (2317)**, Quanta (2382), Wistron (3231), WiWynn (6669), Accton (2345), Inventec (2356), and Delta Electronics (2308). International heavyweights such as NVIDIA, Google, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, and Intel will also attend. Key focus areas include AI clusters, advanced packaging, thermal management, open data center power architecture, and optical networking.

high.title: Apple Earnings Expected to Beat Estimates This Week; Taiwan Supply Chain Stands to Benefit
high.summary: Apple is scheduled to report its fiscal Q3 (ending June) results after the U.S. close on July 30 (Taiwan time: July 31 early morning), with results widely expected to exceed both company guidance and Wall Street consensus. Apple had previously guided Q3 revenue growth of 14–17% YoY, implying USD 107–110 billion, with gross margins around 48%. Wall Street consensus sits at USD 108.58 billion in revenue and diluted EPS of USD 1.89. Analysts anticipate that a strong print — combined with optimism around the upcoming iPhone 18 lineup and Apple's first-ever foldable iPhone — will provide a positive catalyst for key Taiwan supply chain names including TSMC (2330), ASE (3711), Hon Hai (2317), and Largan Precision (3008). This earnings release also marks CEO Tim Cook's final conference call before his September retirement, adding strategic interest around successor John Ternus's potential directional signals. **Market Implication:** A beat and positive guidance could serve as a near-term re-rating catalyst for Taiwan's Apple supply chain names heading into H2 2026. Investors should monitor pre-market reaction and commentary on iPhone 18 and foldable iPhone ramp timelines closely.

high.title: Nomura: AI Semiconductors Still Benefiting from Component Shortages, Price Hikes, and Earnings Upgrades — Seven Taiwan Stocks Favored
high.summary: Nomura Securities has released an AI semiconductor sector report maintaining a positive outlook despite recent consolidation in AI-related stocks. The brokerage identifies component shortages, price increases, and earnings revisions as the next wave of catalysts, while flagging cloud hyperscaler capex visibility as the primary risk. Among Taiwan supply chain names, Nomura issues Buy ratings on seven stocks: TSMC (2330), ASE Technology Holding (3711), KYEC (2449), Fong Jun (7769), Chroma ATE (2360), MPI (6223), and Ying Wei (6515). Notably, Nomura highlights that TSMC's revenue and capex guidance both exceeded market expectations, yet the stock declined post-earnings — a historically rare occurrence (only 4 out of 40 earnings calls in the past decade showed this pattern), with each prior instance resolving into a recovery within at least one month. Nomura draws a parallel to July 2024, suggesting current weakness is a consolidation phase before a renewed uptrend. Key headwinds cited include the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surging over 80% in Q2, limited 2028 data center visibility, free cash flow pressure on hyperscalers in 2027, severe component supply imbalances, and rising yields. **Market implication:** TSMC and the broader Taiwan AI supply chain remain structurally favored; short-term volatility should be treated as an accumulation opportunity rather than a trend reversal signal.

high.title: Taiwan Equity Market Faces Heightened Volatility — Three Key Battlegrounds This Week
high.summary: Escalating Middle East tensions and renewed skepticism over AI monetization drove sharp intra-week swings in Taiwan equities last week, with the quarterly moving average becoming a critical technical defense line. Market strategists identify three pivotal events for this week's directional outcome: (1) **CSP mega-cap earnings** — Microsoft and Meta on July 30, Amazon on July 31 are the focal points, with investor scrutiny on whether massive AI capex is translating into returns; (2) **FOMC rate decision** — the Fed's policy stance and forward guidance will set the tone for global risk appetite; (3) **Middle East developments** — any escalation or de-escalation will drive sentiment across energy, defense, and tech sectors. U.S. markets closed weak on July 24, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 4.25%, Nasdaq down 0.64%, TSMC ADR declining 2.93%, and Taiwan index futures dropping 445 points overnight to 43,369. Google's strong earnings were offset by negative free cash flow alongside Tesla, reigniting AI capex return concerns. **Market implication:** Taiwan equities are in a technically vulnerable position; CSP earnings results carry outsized directional risk for TSMC and the broader semiconductor supply chain this week. Fund managers should closely monitor Microsoft and Amazon guidance on AI infrastructure spending.

medium.title: "Swift Dividend Fill" Stocks Deliver Double Returns — Largan, Formosa Petrochemical Gain Over 60% Post-Ex-Dividend
medium.summary: Driven by strong AI demand and upward earnings revisions, Taiwan's equity market has seen exceptional dividend fill performance in 2026, particularly among TWSE 50 large-cap constituents. As of July 24, 38 of the Taiwan 50 constituents had gone ex-dividend, with 11 — including TSMC, MediaTek, UMC, and Yageo — filling their dividends on the same day. Largan Precision (3008), Formosa Petrochemical (6505), and Winbond (2344) surged more than 60% post-ex-dividend, generating both dividend income and capital gains for shareholders. Analysts from KGI, Quanta, Uni-President, and Taishin Investment Advisory attribute the bullish momentum to TSMC's upward earnings revision — now projecting 2026 Taiwan corporate earnings growth of nearly 50%, with another 20%+ growth expected in 2027 — underscoring the durability of the AI upcycle. Domestic retail inflows via regular ETF subscription plans are also providing liquidity support despite continued foreign investor net selling.

medium.title: Delta Electronics Reportedly Signs USD 2 Billion SiC Long-Term Supply Agreement with Infineon
medium.summary: Market sources report that Delta Electronics (2308) has signed a long-term supply agreement (LTA) worth approximately USD 2 billion (NTD 65 billion) with German power semiconductor giant Infineon for silicon carbide (SiC) components — Delta's first such procurement LTA since the COVID-19 pandemic. SiC is a critical material for NVIDIA's AI power architecture transition to 400VDC and 800VDC systems. Industry observers interpret the large-scale procurement commitment as a sign that Delta has secured meaningful breakthroughs in NVIDIA orders, countering recent market concerns about 800VDC architecture delays that had weighed on Delta's share price. Delta has declined to comment on the report; its investor day is scheduled for July 30, where analysts will focus on 800VDC ramp timelines and the company's solid-state transformer (SST) roadmap. Delta's president has previously stated that SST demand will surge no later than 2027.

medium.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang: "This Time Is Different" — Chip Industry Will Not Enter Downturn in Near Term
medium.summary: In an interview with Axios, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang directly addressed AI bubble concerns, stating that the semiconductor industry will not enter a downturn "for a good while," arguing that current demand is not seasonal or inventory-cycle driven, but rather a fundamental shift in computing infrastructure requirements. Huang projected that the global semiconductor industry must grow five to ten times over the next decade to meet AI infrastructure needs. Taiwan analysts note that Huang's public reassurance helps stabilize market sentiment, and that prolonged chip industry expansion will continue to benefit Taiwan's key semiconductor players including TSMC (2330), ASE (3711), Nanya Science (2408), and Winbond (2344).

medium.title: "Trump Trade" — Once a Market Darling — Now a Significant Underperformer
medium.summary:
Ned Davis Research's "Trump Trade Index" — comprising 12 ETFs tied to housing construction, defense spending, and manufacturing reshoring — has plunged approximately 16% since May after initially outperforming the S&P 500 early in the year. The Iran conflict has driven up energy prices, inflation expectations, interest rates, and the U.S. dollar, undermining the trade's core thesis. Several constituent ETFs including VanEck Rare Earth & Strategic Metals ETF, Global X Uranium ETF, and Global X Defense Tech ETF have turned negative year-to-date after gaining 20%+ in Q1. BCA Research notes that AI-oriented positioning has outperformed at the expense of traditional cyclicals. **Relevance to Taiwan:** The rotation away from cyclicals and defense toward AI-driven tech further reinforces concentration of global flows into Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain, though rising rates and USD strength remain risks for Taiwan life insurers with large USD-denominated foreign investment portfolios.
